Lots of choices but basic choices: Eggs, potatoes, crepes, omelettes(wait in line),bacon, sausages, mushroom soup,  cheese and meat counter with pastries and a couple salads. Presentation was well done. It was good food (nothing over the top or spectacular) but disappointing for 45$ a plate. Nothing French Canadian or Quebec flare about this brunch menu with the exception of the plain crepes(add your own toppings available). Totally over priced for what was there. Atmosphere was really nice staff was awesome!

Made a reservation can get really busy for a Saturday. I tried the lemon poppyseed pancakes as I am a sweet tooth. The fresh berries were so good. I really want to come back to try there dinner time items. 

Lots of parking the place decor is very classic, vintage and rustic. 

Make sure to buy your extra bake goods to take home as soon as you get there. They sell out fast. 

The service was great and it was quite lots at first because it was packed but after 2pm  it got quieter. 

Their plates and cutler have so much character they are all different. 

Can't wait to come back to enjoy more savoury items.

This restaurant is very lovely.  The food is EXCELLENT.  I loved the dim ambiance, the decor and the overall atmosphere.  It's perfect for a date night or even an outing with a group of friends.  5 stars!

I was at today Chartier and had the Duck and Waffles and OMG! Honestly THE best duck I have ever had... So flavourful, moist inside and crispy coating. Amazing waffles and blueberries.... Absolutely knocked brunch out of the park with this dish  

I have to add: the service was over and above. Our waiter was amazing with the kids and was in such a great mood, helpful and patient. Darren himself held an umbrella for the kids and I to get to our car in the pouring rain! This kind of service I expect from places like the Fairmont and we have it in this amazing little town with this high-class little restaurant!
Such a gem in Beaumont. We've enjoyed brunch, lunch, dinner, and burger nights. The bread bar is such a treat - those cronuts are to die for!

This place has a great reputation for good reason. The atmosphere is rustic chic and you would feel comfortable dressed up or casual. I loved everything I had. Our server was great helping us choose a wine by offering samples and answering any questions about the menu. Some items like bone marrow I'm not adventurous enough to try but we started with the homemade bread & butter and mushroom toast, which was very good. I had the Beef Bourgeon and ate every bit of it. One person at our table was admittedly a fussy eater and the chief came and spoke to her personally to adjust the sides to her prime rib dinner. She loved it and found out she loves truffle butter too. My husband is also a fussy eater and didn't love the leeks on the cod. For dessert my husband had the blueberry pie, which was a small entire pie crafted to perfection! I must come back to try the poutine and cocktail creations!

The Chartier has been on my foodie bucket list since last month. So, decided to explore the place with my family on weekend for a brunch. Make sure you get your table reserved on call before heading to Chartier, because they have a long waiting period.
Talking about ambience, their furniture really go along with the dim lights and rustic look. Their crockery collection is also interesting and fascinating. Well, not to forget about the fur covers on chairs. They add up brightness and glow to those chairs. 

Coming to order:
We ordered the delicious large plates by Chartier.
1. Scotch egg: My goodness, this boiled egg wrapped with sausage meat and deep fried with barbecue sauce and mayo tasted so delicious and amazing .
2. Les Oeufs:  A classic english breakfast with egg, sausage and smashed baby potato.
3. Mushroom on Toast Bennie: These sautèed mushrooms and mushroom mousse plate is a perfect to start a day with vegeterian meal.

Crispy smashed baby potatoes served with every plate was actually addiction because they were so delicious and mouthwatering.

Talking about desserts: Check their dessert of the day menu to know more.

Pumpkin spice cheesecake: Well not impressed with the cheesecake being so much sweet. Which somewhere restricts the flavour of cheesecake. 

Rating:
Ambience: 4.5/5
Taste: 3.5/5 
Portion size: 3/5 (There were more of baby potato as side dishes rather than the main dish, which could be improved)
Staff: 4.5/5 ( Courteous and polite)
Presentation: 4/5 ( Liked the cheesecake jar)

If you're wondering if brunch here is worth a trip out to Beaumont, lemme tell you now... IT IS. Although it was mainly street parking I saw, there were a few spots available. We also made reservations on the day of and just 30 minutes prior to arrival since my little one was at a birthday party and I was craving something beyond fast food on a Saturday. The interior is quite cozy, rustic, but with elegant touches, and mismatched chairs that all suits the cabin like theme. Service is quick, friendly, and very helpful with assisting (we had asked for extra napkins, cutlery, and a couple other things with our messy little one). 
The food here though... it's next level... from presentation, texture, and taste; it's very unique and memorable. We had the scotch egg, mushroom benedict toast, and pain perdu. And; because the entrance doubles as their bakery, we took home 2 orange creamsicle cronuts...yes I typed right: CRONUTS...available locally here! The food is so impressive here, I cannot find words that would properly describe it, but it's absolutely a restaurant gem in Beaumont and I'd love to come back to try their other dishes during their lunch or dinner times.

What a little gem in Beaumont. The freshly baked sourdough paired with Foie Gras was amazing and the Beets Napoleon was absolutely delicious. I thoroughly enjoyed the Duck and Perogies which was a perfect blend of sweet and savoury. My husband had the Elk Shoulder on Mushroom Risotto, it was so tender and flavourful. I cannot believe what a nice little spot this is just a few minutes away from the city.

This place is fucking fantastic! 5 stars. But unfortunately no photos because I was busy stuffing my face!

I met my brother in-law and his kids out here for brunch on a Sunday morning... it was packed! Beaumont's an interesting town... I'm not saying I was the only minority in the restaurant. But I was the only minority in the restaurant... fortunately enough unlike my review of "The Peaks" restaurant everyone here is extremely friendly! You're treated like family here and the service is incredibly attentive.

I ordered the Mushroom Benny... and it was delicious. The hollandaise sauce is incredibly milky and smooth as well as rich and full of flavour. The other sticking point of this restaurant is that it IS kid-friendly. BUT you wouldn't imagine that. The interior is gorgeous and the details in the restaurant design are very meticulous-- the owners really do care.

I will definitely be back here for dinner seeing how brunch was spectacular!

After hearing so many mixed reviews about this restaurant, we decided to finally just try it. Unfortunately, it was not great. The restaurant is located inside a bar, like you'd have no idea there was a Chinese restaurant inside it. The food was just okay. The ginger beef was not good. It tastes like they used the same oil to fry seafood in. The honey garlic chicken was crispy but the sauce was very thin and hardly had any garlic flavor. The shanghai noodles were mostly bean sprouts with a few pieces of cabbage and chicken scattered in. The sauce has real potential if they cooked it a little longer so it became thicker and actually coated the noodles. Green onion cake was subpar. Spring rolls were crispy but had a weird after taste. Honestly, this place could become a real competitor for Chinese food in Beaumont if they just stepped up their game. Fresh veggies in the noodles, changing oil or dedicating one fryer to seafood only, putting some thought and care into the dishes.

Very cosy place in the French section of Greater Edmonton. Interieur is a blend of a barn, log cabin and bar, but then food is served on porcelain from your French grandma in Europe. Delicious food. Friendly staff. Fast service. No American Express cards unfortunately.

Run, do not walk, to Chartier.  Our group of six had the pleasure of dining there on a bustling Saturday evening and we are already planning our next evening there.  I should say from the outset that we were a complicated group: many allergies and dietary restrictions.  We wrote to the restaurant ahead of time to ask if our restrictions could be accommodated and the entire staff was open and responsive, modifying existing menu items for sensitivities to wheat, onions, soy, and dairy.  The chef even offered to make a special dish for some of us.  We ended up declining the offer only because he was so open to making minor changes to the very appealing existing dishes.  The results--both the regular and modified items--were outstanding.  The smoked flank steak was perfectly cooked and beatifully flavored with diced bacon, vegetables and a reduction; the beef tartare was out of this world; even the bread and butter were sublime.  Several of us chose (and loved) the very rich beef bourguignon and more wishes they had selected the inventive savory pumpkin pie.  (Me, I'm going back for the lobster at some point). Those of us who enjoyed dessert went for the tarte au sucre (with perfectly tender crust and smooth filling) and the hot chocolate (decadently chocolatey with homemade marshmallows).  The service was attentive without ever being overbearing and every part of our dining experience was simply a treat.  For me, Chartier ranks as high on my list of favorite Edmonton restaurants as Corso 32 and Uccellino (albeit with a very different and more casual vibe).  If you love a fantastic restaurant, this place is for you.

It's taken me a year and the Anthony Henday completion to get down to Chartier in Beaumont and I should have come earlier! This place is a gem and I will be back very soon. 
It's worth the drive from North Edmonton to get a proper 1lb  poutine! The in house baked sourdough bread is exactly how I like it crunchy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. They offer it with a variety of dishes but it's best with the foie gras, herb salt, and balsamic reduction. It's a must have with the mussels as well since the andouille sausage white wine liquid is begging to be sopped up. 
The smoked flank steak with deep fried mash potato balls is also an instant favorite. The cheesy mash oozes out of the crunchy outer shell of tempura and perfectly components the smokey steak cooked to a perfect medium rare. 
Ending the meal with two house made truffles was perfect since we were soo stuffed from the previous 6 courses! Each small bite of truffle was rich, smooth and creamy. 
We didn't try any of the cocktails but that will have to happen on our next visit. The wine by the glass selection was small but seemed thoughtful.
The ambiance starts with the outer facade which makes you think of Montreal with the exposed brick. The theme continues when you enter and you're greeted with a warm cozy atmosphere filled with amazing aromas, friendly smiles and contented appetites. I shall return post haste!

Went for steak and frites night for my wife's bday, nothing but good things to say. Service was awesome, the steak feature was unreal, drinks were great, and they let us bring our own cake and no charge. Thank you for another great experience!!
Best restaurant around by far.

My daughter and I had a great experience Tuesday evening at Chartier!  Our first trip ever to the restaurant and our experience started off with a very warm welcome from all staff; we found them to be so well trained and we knew with that start that we were in for a treat!

So nice to sit down and be welcomed right off the bat with a complimentary little " slate board" each; with a tasting of their cheese featured on their charcuterie board.  Nothing like enjoying a glass of wine and a tasting of local cheeses while we made our made menu selections!

The whole meal was awesome ! There were so many good choices we decided to share several!We started with their sourdough bread, butter & salt board, Chartier, Steak tartare delicious, tempura green beans with Maple syrup served in a Maple syrup can! Very good, and you can see, in our photos, three amazing choices we made ,out of many, for our dessert.

Overall a really wonderful experience and can not wait to return!

I have so much to say about both dinner and brunch! This French-Canadian restaurant in the town of Beaumont is worth the trip! First off, Beaumont is nowhere near as far as I thought it would be. It's a half hour away from the downtown core. It's also a hop, skip, and jump away from anybody residing south of the river. Get yourself onto the Henday and you're golden. 

A straight road once you turn south onto 50th Street, Chartier is located right in the heart of Beaumont. The interior space is rustic and in the quaintest way possible: old church pews, barnwood scavenged from the area, and lovely incandescent lighting decorate the room. There's even a feature wall with the names of all their Kickstarter supporters! 

For dinner: Coho Salmon Ceviche with charred fresh ramps, grapefruit slices, and sourdough bread and salted butter. I was happy to see local business Effing Seafood spread his love all the way to Beaumont! 

The Pork Jowl Cakes came out next and both Diane and I were swooning at just the plating of it. Pork jowl (or cheek) is one of my favourite parts of the pig! Pan fried and formed into cakes, this was one of the most memorable dishes for the night. I was surprised by the lack of fillers used in the cake -- amazing amount of tender pork crammed into a taste bomb. Combined with a black pepper jam and an apple rocket slaw, this dish really took it to the next level, a well-balanced bite of tart, sweet, savoury and also the arugula's pepperiness. Is that a word? 

You can't really go to a French-Canadian restaurant and not order the Poutine. Our appetizer sized Canadian staple came with triple-cooked handcut french fries, cheese curds, and a gluten-free Montreal gravy. The menu says it's "magic" and I believe it. Cheese curds currently not made in house quite yet but they were squeaky so I was happy! It's the fries that get all the love, the best bits and pieces being the ones with crispy skin. 

Crispy Duck. The dish was true to its description, crispy (and apparently, gluten-free!). The use of blue cheese and rosemary in the ganache was pleasant as a sauce although hard-pressed to find if I hadn't reread the menu. It was also described with sriracha, which surprisingly didn't overpower any other flavours in the dish, albeit question usage in a French-Canadian restaurant. I didn't know what to think about the smoked broccoli, although I think personal taste really comes to play as Diane absolutely loved it!

Tourtière, a meat pie with bison, pork, and confit duck. The pie crust was flaky, the fillings well mixed and tender. Served with brussel sprouts and a housemade rhubarb relish, this was a winning dish!

Usually cubed and braised in a red wine sauce to make a stew, I wasn't expecting a bigger cut on our Beef Bourguignon plate. Because I already had that visualization in mind, I thought the dish needed a touch more sauce or moisture. Granted, when eaten with the smashed pear and bacon roasted mushrooms (oh lordy!), the entrée was much better. A kudos to whoever peppered the dish, seriously makes a world of difference!

Tarte au Sucre comes with a housemade salted whiskey ice cream. I mean, come on. The flavours were on point and the texture of the ice cream was smooth. It's a butter tart cousin and perfect for those with a sweet tooth.

Chartier's Creme Brûlée rotates flavours and that night's feature was orange. Our custard was perfectly set and smooth, creamy in consistency and had a great vanilla flavour. I found it difficult to find any citrus notes from my bites that night but neither of us seemed to mind.

For brunch, I went with my boyfriend and we both started off with local roaster Iconoclast coffee. Eggs Donovan: poached eggs with shaved Montreal smoked meat, pickle, and a delightful dijon hollandaise over a housemade English muffin. I'm not the biggest fan of mustard but the amount of dijon is just right on this dish. 

I didn't think it was too early for a bit of Duck and Waffle, the chicken-alternative being my favourite for any time of day. Might have bit off more than I could chew (physically), the dish is massive! As Chef Brochu stated as the dish came out, "It's a bit fiendish." But OH MAN, was it good. A sweet Cap N' Crunch crusted duck thigh, whole wheat waffle, and berry preserve with thickened maple syrup, the dish comes across like it would be a sugar high but was actually quite savoury. I had to keep fighting away Joe's fork as it reached over to steal a waffle square numerous times. I don't even know if I want to try anything else on the brunch menu... how can you top this??

Okay, maybe you can. We ended up taking a Cinnamon Bun for the road. I don't know how people will take it when I say this, but I think Cinnzeo cinnamon buns are the bomb. And never have I tasted a restaurant-made cinnamon bun that has come close to it until now. Chartier's cinnamon bun is perfect. I kid you not. 

Thumbs up all around for food, atmosphere, and service for Chartier!

YUMMY!! We don't go out a lot so this was a special occasion. It did not disappoint. Rustic, welcoming feel, friendly and our server, Shawn, was SO helpful and provided excellent service. The food was amazing, the drinks were very tasty, the dessert was heavenly. The portions vs price point was surprising. Smaller than expected but that is why we had room for dessert. Totally delicious. We WILL be back... after we have saved up for our next visit.

Fantastic restaurant in a quaint little town! This place has a relaxed, rustic chic vibe. I absolutely looove the decor! 
I recommend making a reservation as it seems to be a busy place but we did a walk in and sat at the bar as it was only 2 of us. 
They have a decent beer selection (local) and based on what I saw on the wall behind the bar, decent scotch selection as well.
Everything on the menu sounded deliciously decedent but I decided on the breakfast poutine and cappuccino and the boyfriend got a coffee and les oeufs. 
The poutine had the biggest cheese curds I have ever seen and they were so fresh! Quite literally the best poutine I have tasted! The gravy was the real deal and the potatoes were crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside. It came with a poached egg topped with truffle hollandaise. Mmm mmm so good! 
The sourdough toast that came with my boyfriend's breakfast was fresh and rustic. It came with a side of fresh raspberry rhubarb jam which was a nice mix of sweet and tart (which they sell at the door and we ended up buying a jar of). 
The service was great and the food was so yummy! We are actually goinback next weekend with friends. THAT is how good it is!

Giving this restaurant five stars even though there were a few things that would normally get a four star rating from us because the service was fantastic and the food pretty delicious. 
Firstly, our reservation ran late.. we were given the option of sitting at the bar and waiting for our table or sitting at a raised table and having dinner there.  We chose the latter because it wasn't a huge deal but I'm sure there are lots of people who would prefer a table or booth. 
Our waiter, Sam, was awesome and didn't say anything when I used my finger to finish off the foam in my husband's drink (if he saw!)
Drinks: Jam Sour, Anna's Amerovole, Jules Blossom and 'Ti Punch. The Jam Sour was husband's favorite and mine was the Anna's. Tequila, Limoncello, Pomegranate & Blueberry. So yummy!
For appetizers, we shared the poutine and French onion soup.  The gruyere (?) on the soup was divine.. I picked it off the side of the bowl.  
For dinner we had Tortiere and the Redtail Beef Bourguignon.  I had originally wanted the Beaumont Smoked Meat Sandwich but they were sold out. Tortiere was good.. had an earthy taste and flaky crust.  Brussel sprouts on top were amazing. 
The Bourguignon was cooked really well but the cold pear on top and apple sauce were meh. Didn't love the hot/cold temperatures together. My husband ate the mushrooms/bacon before I even got to try them. 
For dessert, the Pouding Chomeur was recommended and did not disappoint. I dont love apples but my husband does.  I ate around them... the sucre a la creme sauce on top was delicious with the mascarpone mousse (I could eat a full bowl of those two things together).
Overall, the food was incredible and worth the few little "off" things. 
Will be back!
This place has great food and service.  Fresh and tasty.

I had been wanting to try this restaurant but was hesitant as it's on the complete opposite side of the city from me. 

After putting it in the GPS, I saw that Beaumont really wasn't that far so we made a reservation a couple of weeks in advance. When you first walk up to Chartier, you feel the warmth and excitment coming out of the restaurant. Inside, the decor is chic with touches of French heritage. 

Upon recommendation, we had the fresh bread as an appetizer and added on the bruleed brie. I have dreams about this dish. It was the perfect combination with the maple butter and herbed salt. The bread was a fresh sour dough that wasn't over powering in taste. 

Unfortunately, we were disappointed with our main dishes. We tried the smoke meat sandwich and the beef special (a large cut of steak). The smoke meat was pretty fatty and didn't measure up to the Montreal version. The steak ended up being more fat than meat and had a slightly plastic taste to it - possibly because it was cooked sous vide?

I will definitely be making the drive out again  just for that bread and appetizers because it definitely filled you up!

I finally made it to this restaurant, which I have been hoping to get to for quite a while! A friend of mine Pierre lives in Nisku suggested we meet there, and I was like let's do it!

That's quite a price with the ambiance in the decor, it's a lot more cosy than I thought it would be. Do you think got some really nice sheepskin for is on each table in case you get a little cold.

She need you walk in there's a bit of a bread store, where they're selling breads and pastries... Really cool touch, and I'm sure does well in Beaumont for that.

I will deathly be back for dinner but this time just had some drinks and some small plates. The selection of craft beer on tap was awesome, and we need of having the muscles which were cooked to perfection. So tender and really nice flavors. There's also a daily special which was some deep-fried smelts, which I haven't seen in a very long time on a menu so I definitely jump at that. It was done really nice on toast and was cooked delicately.

Definitely will be back for dinner... Can't wait to try the Beef Bourguignon and other French favs!

Had this place ear marked for quite sometime now. If you don't mind making your way out to the quaint little town of Beaumont, this place is worth checking out.

Probably the neatest space I've seen in a while. Lots of wood tables, old school chairs, excellent art and the lighting really ties it together. It definitely tight but at the same time you don't feel cramped. 

So this is basically a riff off of a Quebec style restaurant with a menu offering a higher end twist to some French Canadian classics. The menu is split into small plates on one side and large on the other. This is misleading! 

So I decided to go with the poutine on the small and the classic tourtiere off the large. The girlfriend went with Kentucky fried mushrooms off the small and a French veggie medley of the large. Now her portion for the mushrooms was about right. 5-6 pieces with a lovely chili dipping sauce. Pretty good. My portion was absurdly huge. Beware if you order the poutine as your starter, it's about 2 lbs worth of spuds, gravy, and cheese curds. All pretty good nothing spectacular. A heads up would've been helpful but ok. 


Then the mains...her vegetables were awesome! I didn't try any cause after the giant poutine I was worried about even getting this tourtiere down. It's a giant piece for sure with shaved brussel sprouts and mashed potato's. More potatoes welp! I've had a few tourtiere's before and loved them every time. This one not so much. It was a great pastry crust filled with ground bison chuck, confit duck, and ground pork. Unfortunately it was so heavily spiced with cinnamon and clove it's all you could taste. It was so cloying on the palate I couldn't even enjoy my awesome bottle of vino we brought. My whole mouth was coated. I'm sure there's some traditionalists out there would disagree with me but that's not like any tourtiere I've ever had. 

Our service was absolutely impeccable. We had a great guy that was extremely knowledgeable about where the food came from and knew the menu like the back of his hand. Great great job. Another great thing about this place is the corkage rate. Only 25 bucks a bottle if you bring a bottle of Canadian wine. Done and done!

For me this probably a 3.5 star place for this time out. Definitely a place to go to if you haven't been. If you don't like clove, stay away from the meat pie. But I would definitely give this place another try at some point.

Cheers

Andy

Lunch date with hubs last week, took a day off when kids back at school. Made the +25 min drive out to Beaumont for lunch. I had high expectations for this place given reviews and rewards. Decor was rustic Canadiana. Lunch menu smaller than evening service. Servers were friendly. Their food is IG worthy, however my 2.5 out of 5  review next explains Chartier could be even better if... 

We started off with mussels, the sourdough bread to soak up the cheesy sauce was good. Some of the mussels were not fully open, we could have sent back but then would have added to the delay for the rest of our lunch. That Tuesday's lunch crowd was ok, not full house but the kitchen was really slow. Maybe the slowness of our order was due to the lobster mac-n-cheese?!? This dish was one of their most popular, but it so needed more lobster. 45 min wait, one small claw in a tiny skillet of cheesy pasta for $19. This dish was not worth the hype. 

Hubs' smoked meat sammie with side salad was also interesting. Zero  for sandwich presentation, came out by itself on a plate wrapped in butcher paper. Why? We were eating in not taking away! And such a waste of paper, they could have used sandwich parchment instead (if purpose was to keep hands clean) and had served the sandwich cut open on the plate with the salad on side. The side salad had enough shredded cheese to take over any greens that was supposed to be a salad. We're veterans to smoked meat sammies on our travels. Chartier's smoked meat was pretty good, but over powered with the grainy mustard and pickles. The pickles needed to be on the side. 

Overall food was ok, it needs work in timing and presentation if I'm comparing other Québécois cuisine establishments. Perhaps this is the "Prairies version" and that's the best we'll get. I'd have to be strongly convinced to return for a meal, as this lunch with drive was almost 2.5 hours. Sorry but not worth my time Chartier lovers.

Worth the 45 min drive for me! I had a Caesar which was perfect with just enough spice, my friend and I shared a poutine (it could have had more cheese and thinner fries but otherwise it was very delicious), I had the beef bourguignon which was perfectly cooked and the bacon and mushrooms that came with it were very delicious. Then I had the molasses brown bread pudding. I was a little skeptical about the blueberries with it but it was just perfect. Service was great- my water glass was never empty, and the atmosphere is rustic and comforting with the lights dimmed. I thoroughly enjoyed Chartier and absolutely recommend it.
Quite a surprise in Beaumont.. Really enjoyed the food and atmosphere, comes with a good price point as well

This is a jewel of a restaurant in Beaumont. The food was great and the menu had a variety of options. The staff was super friendly. I can see why this restaurant is such a popular place. My only downside was I found the prices to be on the high side.
Charming restaurant, has the feel of old Quebec. Great food and service, excellent venue for date night.

Loved it fully, was with wife for an anniversary dinner. We are not too familiar with French food. Sloane (a Celtic name) was extremely helpful with a sweet smile and helped us overcome our ignorance. Ultimately had a good sampler of many things. Specially loved the Beef Bourguignon and the onion soup and yes the wine and cocktails.
Will surely visit again

This place is my go to before shopping at the outlet. We live in the northside and each time i try something new out of the menu. I had their breakfast poutine and hubby had the reuben. Both were delicious. We shared both dishes and we were so full that we didn't have room for dessert. The good news was they have a bread window where you can take home their baked goods. Who can honestly pass up a CRONUT with cookie dough filling. We took a sourdough bread and some cronuts home. 
I just love the ambience of this place, cozy and classy. Then the impeccable food and attentive customer service makes that 45 minutes drive well worth it.

The best restaurant have ever been there for a long time! Ce restaurant canadien francais offre des ingrédients frais et délicieux.Tout est fait maison. Meme le pain! J'ai essayé le brunch et le lunch..c'était excellent! Le prix est correct, vu la qualité des produits. Bon choix de menu. Bon choix de consommation. Je recommande ce restaurant a tout le monde. Ça vaut le détour!
Excellent service and venue is wonderful. Lunch had smaller plates but were tasty.  Yes will go again for dinner.

The restaurant itself not as nice as we would have thought it to be given all the hype reviews. Lots of shorts, t-shirts and ball caps as attire so no need to change to dine here. The green beans on the rib-eye steak dish were cold. We sent the dishes back and they returned as they should be with appropriate apologies. Tiny bit of bread to go with the oyster/clam appetizer. Asked for more which was brought. Much to later dismay, was charged for :(  Main dishes were fine if unspectacular. Duck and pancake dinner a definite miss although highly recommended by waitstaff. No decaf coffee to be had. Out of blueberry pie. Served dessert with joke souvenir tiny spoons claiming that was all they had. Scooping lemon dessert from mason jar with baby spoons did not leave a good taste in our mouths for the whole experience. Mostly good food. Probably would not return.

Best experience in a long time!!!! This is a wonderful place!!!! Everyone is very friendly and welcoming!!! The food is amazing!!! You need to order 2-3 dishes because there are not that big but delicious!!! 
The salads are soooo good!!!!!! There are my favourite!!!

We will be back!!!
great meal - I entertained a colleague from Austria and this was a great example  of  local food.  We enjoyed the ambiance of the room and it was a great evening.

They make a lot of the components for their menu items in house so the flavours are unique and exceptionally good. The atmosphere is very relaxed and you are not rushed through your meal. Prices are slightly higher than normal but for the quality of the food they are very fair. Had the BLT and it was great, can't wait to try the smoked meat sandwich next time.

The food is good, the service charming, the decor fun. The volume is loud on a Saturday night, the portions small, the place is busy. 
The ambiance is fun, friendly and quirky. What's with the no major labels of pop?  Was there the first week it opened, and bugs were being worked out. Went again recently, and it was much smoother. Will go again for sure.

I like this place. From the mismatched dinnerware to the mismatched chairs etc the atmosphere is really cool, if a little loud. The service is really good. I've been here a few times, but only for brunch (definitely going to try it for dinner) and it's been good. This time I was with my mom and had the Tomato Tartine and really enjoyed it - two little suggestions - a little bit more flavour (thin sliced red onion, maybe?) and please, a steak knife. The toasted sourdough bread is a little bit hard to cut with a butter knife. The side salad was good, but also a little bit bland ...  Mom had the Les Oeufs and enjoyed it.  Really like the jam and the sourdough.  Eggs were done just right and she said the sausage was really good.  All in all, worth the visit.  Dinner next !!

Chartier is simply magnifique! Everything about this lovely French restaurant is delightful from its fresh bread to its small but varied menu to the mismatched mugs that accompany an altogether quaint atmosphere. 

I went for brunch and the smell of fresh bread was still wafting throughout the restaurant as we sat down. The menu was divided into small plates (such as cinnamon buns and  poached egg inside a bacon glazed bagel) and big plates (featuring omelettes, fresh sausage and eggs benedict).  Each item on the menu looked incredibly tasty and while there weren't a great deal of vegetarian optionsI was pleased nonetheless to see a few tasty offerings. 

You can tell that each ingredient listed on the menu was carefully and deliciously prepared, ranging from bacon maple glaze, to whipped cream cheese to smoked dill and other fresh cheeses. The freshly baked sourdough is flavourful, chewy and might just be the highlight of the whole place. You can also get their bread from a bread window if you get there in time on certain days!

The service, brunch food and atmosphere were all fantastic and I'd happy make the trip out to Beaumont to visit Chartier again for any meal!
The service and food were excellent.   Definitely recommend the poutine and the peach donut

Chartier was recommended to me by a colleague, so I decided to surprise my husband a few weeks ago with brunch. Apparently this place has enough of a reputation that when I said we were going to Beaumont, the surprise was ruined. Oh well!

The restaurant has a shabby chic atmosphere complete with mismatched chairs and dining-ware but it was just the right amount of cute. The staff were friendly and especially helpful in locating us a spot in the corner where we could have baby (who was sleeping) close, but not in the way. While there were other noisy children that day, ours certainly wasn't one of them :)

The food was good but nothing overly memorable - I had "the eggs" - Hubby had the Duck and Waffle. And because we just couldn't help ourselves, we brought home a cinnamon roll (sampling a bite before packing it up.) Overall the food and atmosphere felt like somewhere back home in Kentucky and I found a lot of comfort in that. I did not however, sense any French flare. Perhaps we need to return for dinner to get the full experience!?!

My wife tells me we're going to dinner at a French restaurant, and I think... where is there a French restaurant in Edmonton? Well, it's not technically in Edmonton but it's in a small town just south east about 30 minutes outside of Edmonton in Beaumont. It's a beautiful small town that's got a quaint main street like many similar sized towns. Near the middle of town, we find Chartier on the main street through town. There is parking in the back as the parking in the front of the restaurant is often hard to find when it's busy. 

When you walk into the restaurant, the first thing you see is a wall of fresh daily baked breads that you can purchase and take home to enjoy. Right after you pass the entry way there's a long bar and an open space with tables of different sizes. We were seated a bit further back near the kitchen that had a window probably for serving and convenience but it allowed for open views into the prep area, which for some might be a plus. All the chairs at the various tables were different sizes and styles which sounds bad but in this space it worked and fit with the decor of the space. In our party of four we decided on 4 different large plates, the Beaumont Smoked Meat Sandwich with a side of poutine (at an additional cost), the Tourtière, the Wholey Cow special (which was a burger when we went) also with a side of poutine, and a seafood bisque served with 3 buns made in-house. 

The smoked meat sandwich was something that you'd expect to find in a Montreal deli complete with brisket, served on sourdough bread, dijon mustard and pickles. It was a decent sized sandwich and was more than filling enough for a dinner portion especially when coupled with a small poutine. I'd go back for this sandwich alone because it was delicious (at least the small portion I was able to have had shared with me). The tourtière is a bison meat pie, that was also a large portion more than enough to fill my friend who ordered it. He stated that he loved it granted he had been craving this for a while so that might have made him biased to it all. My wife had ordered the burger with the side poutine. The burger was very juicy and thick, it was a bit tall to eat comfortably, and it did sort of fall apart near the end but the taste was still there and she would order it again.  The poutine was a bit salty and didn't quite meet our expectations for poutine but it wasn't bad per se, it's just that everything else was just that much better. I had the seafood bisque which looked very rich and creamy however it didn't feel heavy at all, the seafood tasted fresh and nothing was terribly over powering which is a good thing, and the buns that came with bisque were just heavenly. Hot, fresh and fluffy were such a great to have with butter or eat as a vessel to dip the bisque. 

Throughout the meal we were attended to often but not so much that it felt annoying. The wait staff were always friendly and engaging in conversation but it never felt forced. The overall experience was great and I would definitely be going back for special occasions or other things to celebrate because it is a bit pricey but worth the money. Check back with them frequently as they do change their menus every so often. Just for reference I went here almost a month or so ago and since I've gone they have changed a few menu items.

I was torn between a 4.5 and a 5 star rating.. but can't figure out how to give half a star so here it is... 5 stars!!

There has been a tonne of hype since this place opened and personally I didn't get caught up in it... like really, how good could it be for our little town? Then I had the opportunity to go with my friend for my birthday dinner and I have to say how impressed I was.

If you're nit picky about matching, then I wouldn't recommend this place as it'll drive you nuts as all of the plates, cups, etc are a hodge podge of mixes. Really, who cares - they're clean :)

We started off with the tempura beans and I have to say - WOW! They were so delicious, I could have ordered a couple of orders and just had that for dinner. I will definitely be back, if not just for the tempura beans.

My friend ordered the chicken which was good.. juicy and large portions. I had the steak, which after eating sooooooo much turkey for Christmas, I really appreciated. It was delicious and so were the parmesan fries that it came with. I took leftovers home and ended up eating them for breakfast as I couldn't wait till lunch to finish them off!

Our server was nice and considering how packed the place was, the service was great... and the food came out of the kitchen fast! It has definitely given the people of Beaumont the option of a great meal without having to drive to Edmonton... which I appreciate.

Food was excellent.  Staff were awesome and friendly. 

The only complaint was the loudness.  We took an elderly lady and it was too loud for her.

Worth the drive out from Edmonton.  Very imaginative brunch menu and you can taste the homemade - I had the Scotch egg and it was almost too much but wth the help of my husband I polished my plate.   Very nice personal service from the co-owner and charming wait-staff.  The decor is fun - Urban meets Western.

Outstanding....mushroom and cabbage appetizer, the bread, the beef bourgionion and salmon! What service, what atmosphere, but the food! Taste, presentation and price, it's all here. A must visit, worth the drive. Oh..,and creme brûlée

Service and food was good. We were a bit disappointed in the main meal. Our friends ordered the small plate poutine which was huge. My wife and I each ordered  the poutine a rosenau (a "large" plate dish). Our poutine was tiny, especially in comparison to the small plate version. The poutine a rosenau was also not very good. There was almost no lobster in the chowder layer (not even a full bite of lobster), the bread was impossible to cut, and there were only a few fries and cheese curds. To top it off, it was $28, compared to the small plate poutine that was more than double the size for $10. Coming from Quebec, we were disappointed in this poutine, and think the combination didn't work. The prices make you feel like it will be a fancy resto with fancy food, but fails to meet the price in quality. To end on a positive, the crispy duck appetizer was delicious and we would definitely order it again.

I have to say I was disappointed with my first visit to Chartier on Sunday. I had heard great things but it was pretty average overall. Most disappointing was the quantity of the seafood special: 5 scallops and 3 (small) mussels...for $37. Don't get me wrong: it was delicious. But it was more an appetizer than an entree. I had to order the poutine to top me up. 

The service was good, the place is nice, but the special needs some work. 

My wife's beef Bourgognon (?) was also good...but not great. Good flavour. 

Oh..and the poutine was okay...not as good as the same at Cafe Bicyclette in Edmonton's French Quarter. 

I'm not sure we would return, to be honest.

Between the fresh bread and foi gras, the tempura beans, and the tourtière, the food was delicious and authentic. Have been there for both such and supper and have been very pleased with the service and the food. Only negative is the noise level can get very high when the restaurant is full.
Love this cozy, unique restaurant with excellent food. A star out in the burbs definitely worth the ride.

I will start by saying that a 5 star restaurant to me means it is world class. Maybe I am a huge snob.....whatever.

I went to Chartier as part of a party of 7. We had a tasting menu at the chefs table and we were hosted by one of the owners, Darren.

The service was very warm and friendly. Darren made everyone feel relaxed. It was more like going to a friends house for dinner. There was perfect balance between being friendly, but with excellent service.

The room is super interesting it feels warm and rustic, but still elegant and classy somehow.

It gets a little loud. Most people would not notice, but I have trouble hearing when there is a ton of ambient noise. Too many metal concerts in my youth. It seems these days, people love the noise. It is common in many restaurants, it seems and that is ok because it lends to the positive energy of the place.

The food. They do homemade bread here and it is amazing! Really! We have seven dishes and all left very full. At the beginning, Darren said, "Tasting menus are usually small portions, but we are not doing that. Tonight, you eat!"

Every dish was very good to excellent. Our group was very happy and there were many oooooos and aahhhhs. If I were to critize anything, it would be that many dishes felt very carb-heavy. I love carbs, but it affected the balance a little. Flavours tended towards the sweet side, which is definitely in tune with a lot of places these days. I found the flavours very complex. Perhaps to the point where the main ingredients were overshadowed. Dishes were delicious still - I think if I were ordering one dish, rather than sampling so many, this would be welcome.

The only thing our group truly felt was off was the music. It was some sort of odd 90s playlist which did not feel fitting in the surrounding, nor the sophistication of the food. Kind of like nursery rhymes playing at a high school dance. 

Now that is a pretty minor thing. It was our only complaint and it was not so off putting that it affected our dining experience.

I will end with this.

If you want great food, excellent and friendly service in a beautiful and interesting room - go to Chartier. I am a huge food snob and I loved it!
Kevin

Absolutely fabulous food, the poutine was amazing, the beef bourguignon was delicious and the creme brûlée was to die for! Great job all around, the ambiance is fabulous, with a beautiful rustic charm.  I will be back over and over:-)

So very disappointing! We spent over $50 for the worst Chinese food I've ever had. Ginger beef was dry and tasteless. Salt and pepper shrimp disgusting. We're fans of Chinese food and have enjoyed it all over the world...unfortunately NOT in Beaumont!

We have been to a Chartier several times being fortunate to live in Beaumont. Most recently we attended "burger night" . The French onion burger, chicken burger and the classique we all fabulous ! Keep up the great work Chartier!

I've visited this place twice and now. It has been amazing both times. The first time I had the Beef Bourguignon(or however you spell it) and it was fantastic. I had the tempura green beans and duck appetizer. The tempura beans were great but the duck came with some mixture that has beets in it, and I don't care for beets so it was lost on me. Didn't care for it. During my second visit, I had the rabbit leg and it was also pretty great. If I had to pick I'd say the beef was better though. Also, had the mussels appetizer and those were epic. The best of the 3 appetizers I've tried there. Both times the coworker that was with me got the chicken cordon bleu (different guys) and both said it was someo of the best they've had so I'd say it's pretty decent. The drinks are pretty decent as well. Also, service has been consistently great so I would definitely recommend this place for a date night, working lunch or just great culinary experience!

We had such a great meal for our anniversary last night. Everything was perfect...decor, food and our server Max was awesome!!
We will be back
Such a beautifully crafted restaurant, very warm and friendly staff make you feel at home as soon as you walk in. Only tried brunches so far, everything was delicious though!

It had been a while since doing brunch at Chartier and it was as good as I had remembered. The scotch egg was so yummy and the service was good (as per usual). I was a little bummed that the cinniminis had sold out before I had a chance to buy some but that's on me. Go team Chartier!

This restaurant has been recommended to me several times and I finally had the chance to go when my parents came to visit. It was phenomenal from start to finish. We had bread and butter with brûléed brie, haricots verts, chicken cordon bleu sandwich, brisket ragu and the beef bourguignon. All of the food was amazing, our server was very friendly and knowledgeable, the decor and atmosphere is very nice. I love the market and bakery at the front. We got some Saskatoon maple butter tarts on the way out and they were amazing. I'd highly recommend this restaurant and will definitely be back!

This is my favourite restaurant EVER!! It's worth the drive to Beaumont. Everything they make is masterfully thought out. So far I've had their Tarte Au Sucre, Sourdough, Donuts, and Fish and Chips from Effing Seafoods. I really admire that they are so involved in the community and that they support other businesses. They're also featured on "You've Gotta Eat Here" a tv show on Food Network. It's true, you've gotta eat here!!

PRO: The food was legit incredible. I had the Beef Bourguignon, and with all the different ingredients (bacon, mashed potatoes, pear, apple puree) spread out around the meat, it was like having multiple meals at once. Maybe the most flavourful meal I've had in years. 

CON: I felt the prices were quite high. Both our entrees were $29 each. More than I'd prefer (but, if I'm being honest, it was still worth the money)

As much as I would love to write a great review here, I simply find it a bit difficult to do. Loved the place when Steve was the head chef; great concept to start out with; service has always (and continues to be wonderful), but.... And here's where many might disagree - Menu selection just doesn't do it for me. Overall design has gotten tired. Pricing simply asks too much for the return.  Sorry Beaumont fans.

We went here for our wedding anniversary and all the staff were so sweet and congratulated us which was so sweet. We started with a few cocktails that were good but a bit pricey. We started with a delicious Caesar salad that was topped with escargot!!! For our main we decided to be a little crazy and trip the lobster poutine! It was Huge! The lobster was over cooked unfortunately but the homecut fries and the gravy and lobster bisque gravy was to die for!!! Soooo good!!! 

We were too full for dessert but there was some great options!! The atmosphere and the environment in general was so great and a really wonderful spot in a cute little town! Worth the visit and we hope to go back soon!!!

My really good friend funded their Kickstarter so we decided to go for an early meal prior to a concert they were attending on Saturday evening. 

Before I review the food I'm going to say the ONLY reason I didn't give them a 5-star review was because the service was a little on the underwhelming side. We were late for our reservation, so I can understand that is annoying for the restaurant, and we did call and update them on our arrival time twice though. However when we showed up we were reminded twice by the hostesses that we'd need to be done by 6 pm, and then when we were greeted by our server he again reminded us about the fact that they needed us out by 6 pm Then it took ages for them to take our order, and it took well over 20 minutes for me to get my drink because they needed to "change the box" for the cola (which is DELICIOUS by the way). There was also a noticeable lack of experience with our server, but he was friendly and easy to get along with for the most part, just very slow and made some interesting placement and timing choices. 

Now, on to the food! Oh the food! I don't care if you're a 5 star only picky eater or you're a sandwich and fries kind of person, YOU WILL LIKE THIS PLACE. 
Their poutine is spot-on. The fries are the big steak-cut fries, which NORMALLY I am not a fan of, but these ones were cooked PERFECTLY and the gravy was delicious (and it's gluten-free for those of you who are conscious of that). The cheese curds were squeaky and huge and lovely, and that poutine was the things dreams are made of. It was also huge compared to some of their other dishes, so score to that! 

We got the Charcutterie which was Creton (I am French -Canadian so this is my child hood and it was SO GOOD.) Purscuitto and Smoked Meat with house made pickles, jams, comptoes, bread, mustard and some cheeses (an emmental, another I didn't recognize but it was good, and a blue cheese which I avoided like the plague lol) The Charcuterie was a bit less than what I was expecting, having seen photos of other people's, however, it was good none the less. Their smoked meat is delicious and I'm looking forward to coming back and trying the sandwich. 

We ordered the Tomarrow soup which is awesome. That's the best tomato soup I've had in a long time. It was a nice touch being served with the bone marrow and toast. mmm. 

for Mains we got the Tourtiere - because you can't go to a French Canadian restaurant and not. And it did NOT disappoint and the rhubarb jam that came with it was AWESOME. Such a classic dish. I really enjoyed it. 

We got the hen which came with a perfectly cooked egg on top and this Ratatouille that was amazing. The hen itself was 2 small rounds of white and dark meat that were cooked to perfection. Not dry, and Totally full of flavor. 

This restaurant has cane cola on tap and I would totally go there just to get a big-gulp filled if that was socially acceptable. It's delicious. Worth the $3 for a small glass, and I waited for a refill even after we paid because I was not leaving without a second small glass of that amazing soda. 

I'll be going back for sure, and will reassess the service issues we had when we're not on a "time crunch" so to speak.

What a lovely experience. First of all, it gets 5 stars for atmosphere. It is beautiful and intimate. Candles and family photos grace the walls and lots of different spaces to share conversation and have a wonderful night. Our server was excited to serve us. She was prompt, frequent, friendly and informative of the place and of the menu. She gets 5 stars for sure. 
The menu is definatley made for sharing. I thought it was well thought out, but definately made for  heavier dining appetites.  And no seafood. This is where my husband and I come into issues. I don't eat much meat - especially red meat, my husband doesn't enjoy veggies. Usually we compromise on seafood. We both enjoy it. However this menu didn't have a single seafood item on there - no mussles, no shrimp, no clams. I reallly think that perhaps one or two seafood items would be a good addition to their menu and balance it a bit more. We decided on the charcuerie board (I eat the cheese and preserves, hubby eats the meat). The grean beans (because we were assured that they are the most ordered item), and the poutine. I have to say, that the food was good, but not quite as good as I had expected. First of all the charcuerie board was average.  The bread was too thick cut on the platter and not easy to split with all the condiments. The meat and cheeses were fine but nothing stood out as being amazing, and the I felt that the perserves did not pair well with the meat and cheeses we were served. For 34 bucks I would not order this again. I have had much better boards for the same price or cheaper.  Also, the beans were way too sweet for my liking. This may be my own tasts, and if you like sweeter than savory than these you should try. The batter was excellent and the beans well cooked. My husaband  had a token one, and was done. However we packed them up and my teenager wolfed them down. And I thought for the price it was a good serving portion. We both loved the poutine. It was fresh, flavourful and a good deal for 6 bucks. I definatly will try it again and order a few differnt items and hopefully will be wowed. Definatly worth the drive.

This will be a quick and dirty review.

The food was fantastic.  We started with the Poutine and the Haricots Vert.  They were both wonderful, although the beans were a bit on the sweet side.  The wife loved the Hot Hamburger Sandwich, and for me the Beef Bourguignon was beautifully tender and well done. 
They had a number of very different cocktails.....way over priced for what you're getting.  Just because they're a little different, does not mean that you can charge a 50% premium for it.  I would not order any of them again just because of the price.  The wife wanted a coke or pepsi, and then only had Cane Cola???  Very disappointing, and then the server did not make any suggestions aside from alcoholic drinks (obviously I would think that if you're asking for a coke, you don't want an alcohol drink).  after asking about Iced Tea, lemonade etc, she settled for water, but then more than 1/2 way through dinner asked if they had Ginger Ale.  Yup...so why didn't you suggest that in the first place?

The service for food was incredibly slow.  The waitress did apologize several times for the slow service, but blamed it on the large table of guests for slowing the kitchen.  Afterwards however, it came out that it was because of the Chef's table....which should be an expected thing and should have been compensated for.  We got there at 7pm and didn't finally leave until almost 10pm.  Waaaay to long.  Even paying the bill took forever.

The room was nice looking, loved the rustic decor, however.....do something about the NOISE level.  Way Way too noisy, could hardly hear (and the constant repetitive thumping noise coming out of their speakers did not help....very very annoying).  People were practically yelling (some because that's the only way to hear, some because I believe they were drunk).  They have regular tables and a bar in way too small a space.  If you want to have that many tables, then get rid of the bar, and maybe it will cut down on the noise.  Also, put in some ceiling tiles and perhaps wall covering with noise absorption.

To summarize, loved the food.  But with the extremely slow food service, and the horrific noise level, not sure I would go back.  If I could get the same chef at a different restaurant, I'd be there in a heartbeat!

This place really needs to step it up if they want to be in any way competitive. It's by no means the worst take out I've ever had... but it's pretty close. Not only did they get my order wrong but the food quality was very low, especially for the price. The onion cakes were very crunchy, which is usually supposed to be chewy and made me wonder if they just deep fried old onion cakes. The beef had an unusual flavour to it and was quite fatty. After eating multiple people felt sick and really regretted eating the food. Not going to make that same mistake twice.

I recently read about this restaurant online, in an article about the top restaurants in Canada. When I saw that they are located in Beaumont, I got really excited because my sister lives there and I was going to visit her for Christmas. I immediately made a reservation to take my sister for lunch the day I arrived in town. 

When we got there, the restaurant was quite busy. Thank goodness I had made a reservation! We were seated right away and quickly read over the menu. Everything sounded amazing so it was tough deciding what to get. We settled on some mussels to start, followed by their smoked meat sandwich and the lobster mac & cheese. 

The broth with the mussels had bits of chorizo and blue cheese swimming in it. Their house-made sourdough bread was lightly charred and perched on top, still warm from the grill. Perfect for soaking up that delicious broth. 

The smoked meat was accompanied by grainy mustard and crunchy pickles, between slices of sourdough. I discovered they also sell their bread at the front of the restaurant (or at a separate window outside in the warmer months) Of course, we picked up a couple on our way home!

The lobster mac & cheese was my favourite - thank goodness we were sharing everything - I don't think I would've been happy with only a few bites of this. The portion is a good size, and the sauce was creamy and oh-so-cheesy, topped with crunchy panko breadcrumbs. Yum! 

The highlight of the meal for me, the real star of the day, was the dessert. Specifically, the lemon meringue dessert. This was absolute perfection. I will have to find excuses to visit my sister more often, just so I can go back to have this dessert. It was WOW. The lemon curd was sweet and and tart, the texture was nice and smooth, and the shortbread cookie was a stellar choice to have as the crust. All of this was topped by lightly torched marshmallowy meringue and a sprig of mint. For me, dessert doesn't get much better than this.

Our server was very friendly and made some good recommendations. She did forget to put in one of our orders, but was quick to fix it. It was fortunate that we were sharing, though, as one of us would've been eating our entrée alone otherwise. 

It's definitely a bit pricey for the area, but coming from Vancouver and now Toronto, I'm used to seeing more expensive restaurants. I think as people start to have a greater appreciation for high quality food, they won't mind spending a few more dollars for it. 

I really wanted to go back here for dinner but I just couldn't squeeze it in this trip. I will need to go back soon, though, as I'm dying to try their beef bourguignon.

Loved our experience at this brand new restaurant in our hometown. The atmosphere was wonderful, the decor was unique and inviting and the food was delicious. The entire team was extremely engaging and helpful and we are looking forward to visiting them again and again!
Food was amazing, but equally as great was the service and the staff! It was also interesting to learn about the restaurant's history starting off as a Kickstarter campaign. Highly recommend!

Ventured out to Beaumont to try this spot I'd read about online. We went for brunch on a Saturday. Simply outstanding. 

The atmosphere and staff were terrific, the food was excellent and the craft beer selection, although small, was awesome. I love the fact that they have local, and interesting brews on tap. 

We'll be back numerous times I'm sure to try out more of the menu and enjoy some hard to find beer.

I've heard many great things about this place and I was excited to finally try their food. Unfortunately, my dinner experience here was a bit underwhelming. My partner and I made a reservation to eat here at 8pm on a Saturday night. We were seated quickly when we arrived and we can see that the place was filled with people.

We ordered the following:

Mussels Special for the night $14- Mussels were okay. I've tasted better mussels at other restaurants. It tasted full of tomato flavor but I felt like it was missing an ingredient to give it a special kick. 

Redtail Beef Bourguignon $26- I was expecting to be wowed by this dish as many people have posted about it. However it tasted like average braised beef and there wasn't anything that stood out to me from the bites I took from it. 

Sourdough Skinned Salmon $25- I liked the sourdough topping and the maple toasted  pistachios really enhanced the dish. The salmon by itself tasted bland. I liked my first few bites into this dish but by the end, it felt like a chore to finish since the overall flavor tasted odd.

Grapefruit Reverie $10- this was an enjoyable fruity cocktail

Affogato- we ended our night with this dessert. It was a bit small and nothing special.

Perhaps we ordered the wrong food items because this place has so many good reviews. I think I'll come back in the future to try their brunch since their poutine and bread bar looks promising!

Ordered a post-work takeout of the Montreal Smoked Meat and Chicken Cordon Bleu sandwiches and WOW!!!!!! The flavor! The team was amazing to accommodate dietary restrictions too! Just a perfect meal all around!

Lovely restaurant , very pleasant service.My husband and I both had delicious meals , he had beef, said it was very good and I had the salmon which was so so good . Coffee was fresh and nice and hot. We were greeted cheerily and shown to our seats , however they were on high stool type chairs and right in front of the kitchen , not that comfortable and a bit busy . We asked if we could move and we were accommodated , with ease to a better table and more comfortable seating . All in all great little place .
The service, the food and the restaurant are absolutely the best. They have done a phenomenal job of adjust to all the crazy restrictions. This will always be one of my favourite restaurants

This is a nice little restaurant for Beaumont. The wings are always cooked perfectly and they aren't very greasy at all. The wings are kind of small but very tasty. The mystery wings are excellent. And the beer is always icy cold. Thursday night has a beer and wings special that is excellent and they also have 2 for 1 appetizers weekdays before 6pm. (The pickled willies are amazing)

Pleasant bar/pub atmosphere, but in a restaurant setting.  Huge windows letting in lots of light - not the dim lighting one usually gets in pubs.  The décor is country/western, as is the music being played.  Though alcohol is being served, it is a family restaurant.  There are 14 individual wooden tables here plus 3 booths, and a long counter bar with additional seating.  Two tables currently have families with children, the others mostly young folks and a couple of people my age.  (50's)

On a side note, for guys - check out the washroom.  It has the lowest urinal I have ever seen, literally one foot above the floor.  They must serve lots of midgets here.

I was welcomed by a host as soon as I entered, and shown to a table.  Shortly after the waitress (Shannon) came over, offered drinks and informed me of the special.

The menu covers a huge assortment of wings (101 distinct flavors) as well as salads, burgers, ribs etc.  This is my second visit here; I came here the first time roughly a month ago by mistake (?) after having lost my way.  (I'm good at that)

I ordered the 'Spicy Garlic Parmesan' wings.  Yup, I like my food spicy.  It was served within 15 minutes of ordering.  The wings were just awesome; this will be my new favorite location for wings and such.

I have read other reviews of this chain (but none in Beaumont where I visited) mostly complaining about the 'high' prices.  Maybe I make more than most, but I don't consider $15.00 (tax and tips included) to be expensive for a satisfying meal in a pleasant and relaxing atmosphere.  If anything, I would consider that to be darn cheap.
Good wings both dry and wet.  Tasty food including hot dogs and chicken fingers for the kids.  Overall very good food.  Busy place on a Sunday afternoon.
Went here for lunch yesterday. Enjoyed the wings, great selection, food was excellent. Staff were polite and friendly.

Wild Wings, Beaumont is an awesome eatery. We have been coming here on & off since 2013. Wonderful decor & atmosphere. Food is awesome. Beer is even better. We have been here with friends & with family. We will always return. Staff are awesome; great service & sense of humour.

I have traveled around North America allot for work and have had my share of good tacos and beer and this place honestly has the best tacos, damn good beer and super friendly staff if lived here I would be here daily.

I popped in here for a quick birthday get together and was pleasantly surprised at how quick the service was even for as slammed as it was. The Oilers were playing and the atmosphere was buzzing, so if you're around on game night and want a place to watch the game, I'd recommend here... get here early though so you can grab a seat as it fills up quick!

I also have to say how AWESOME Sea Change has been in the Beaumont community! They didn't just come into town and take money. They have been so busy supporting community events and it's AWESOME!! Just for being so active in the community, I'd support them just for that... they really are rockstars!!

Even though I am not a beer drinker (so you're probably wondering why I'd be in a brewery), I still love supporting local business. I also love the fact that there is a tonne of parking as well.

Make sure that you order the chicharrines. It will quickly become your new addiction as they are delicious to snack on!!

This is a newer place in Beaumont, AB that a work colleague invited me to try. This is more pub than restaurant, but it is family friendly - a good concept for a smaller community by not limiting potential patrons. The place is bright, open and friendly!

Sat at the bar as the table and booth seating was full. Every night is wing night here! The first thing I noticed was a sticky bar counter and that immediately turned me off. However, after asking the bartender to give the counter a wipe (which she did) it was explained that the finish on the bar did not mix with the detergent and they were waiting on a new copper bar top. So, will have to come back to check that out!

Beers on tap and by bottle with selection of high balls and wine.

The menu has a variety of pub fare and, of course, a wide selection of wing names (with a feminine slant) and flavours. Tried a garlic and heat along with a teriyaki and heat. Hotness of spice is rated from 1 to 5. I went with 4s. As an appie, I tried a mac and cheese bite. These were interesting - mac and cheese sauce in a deep fried, bite sized "pocket."

Wings arrived -two baskets and a side of fries. The fries are a nice edition! Wings were hot out of the fryer although lacking in spice heat, but tasty nonetheless! Will definitely try "5s" next visit! Give this place a shot!!
Amazing staff and service, keep it up! Huge selection of flavours, it was so hard to decide. Was quite pleased with our food and will definitely be back :)
This places is amazing, food local beer and excellent service, hard to find a place with all this in Edmonton, very very good place

We went to the new Seachange location in Beaumont and had a great experience. I've been twice now, once for drinks and once for drinks and food. The space is average size with a good amount of seating. First time we got stuck at the bar, second time we were able to grab a table.

The beers are amazing and very well priced. The food is also very good. We only had the nachos and really enjoyed them. Next we plan on going for supper/ drinks. 

There are lots of tvs and usually have either the oilers or football playing for you, there is music playing but it's not so loud that you can't talk.

The staff are very friendly and quick to serve. Very good place to go for a night out.

Highly recommend.
Just had lunch again today at wild wings. June 21 2017 and the staff are great, food is excellent and great prices. One of the best places In Beaumont for lunch.

I have always loved wild wings 

Been going there for about a year in the city, and
Now just moving to Beaumont I started going to this one 

The wings are always cooked perfectly

Finally made it out to the Beaumont location... This place is just as good as the original, except bigger, & they have a way bigger menu with some awesome Mexican food!

The beer I think is the best in town, you have to try the wolf, the prairie fairy, and the session ale. The blonde is a really nice basic lager too. Why not try one of everything!

Didn't get a chance to try the food this time, but will for sure in the next time. I absolutely think these guys are killing it when it comes to beer and Edmonton!

Great place for wings and other food, yam fries were good, the lightly seasoned wings were excellent. Drinks were refilled on time. Next time I will chose a different flavor(101) to chose from. Staff was friendly and helpful.

I cannot say enough good things about this butchers. My husband and I have become meat snobs because of this place. We used to get our steaks from Costco, sobeys, or superstore but now we won't even consider it. They get their meat locally from farmers around the area. They even have Kobe style steak. The pork chops are delicious. We've never had any left overs. He can cut any style you want. Tonight he was sold out of tenderloin (which is priced at around $10) and he went back and cut some up for us! Wonderful service and family run!!!

I've came to the Butcher's corner in Beaumont every time I wanted a good steak. I buy my tenderloin and other meats here for camping and BBQing and I always really enjoyed them! I didn't care for their beef jerky though.. But the service is always nice! Everyone is helpful and always seem happy to have your business. Even had the butcher come out and talk with the customers! If you enjoy meat I'd recommend stopping here!

In January 2014 I ordered 25 lbs of honey garlic pepperoni and 25 lbs of maple breakfast sausage from the deer meat I brought in.  Both products taste   outstanding!  My kids eat the pepperoni in their school lunches everyday.  We all look forward to sausages for breakfast on the weekend as that organic meat is much better for you than store bought bacon.

This is like the hidden gem of Beaumont. Open in the summer, she makes shakes and crepes out of her built in kitchen in what was a garage.

Organic eggs and fruit, seats outside. It reminds me of something you would have seen at a drive in movie. The food is delicious, crepes are huge! Love this place!!

Made the trek out to Beaumont today to try this adorable little Crepe shack.

I checked their website first to make sure they were open today and double checked the hours.

Arrived out there to find it closed.  I called the phone number and the voicemail indicated they are closed early for the season in order to work the municipal election.

I was sad that 1) they were closed 2) that I came all the way out to Beaumont and 3) that I'm going to have to wait until Spring.

The courtyard was absolutely adorable and I WILL most definitely be back in the late Spring when they open and hope to have a 5 star rewrite! 

Alas... Winter is coming...

These guys have the best garlic ribs you will find anywhere! They use good cuts of pork and there is no fat or gristle at all. I am also a huge fan of their Mauii style Pork Chops. Again, they use an excellent cut of meat and they are cut to a perfect thickness. The marinade they use is awesome. They taste the best on the barbecue or on a broiler pan in the oven.

This place is so charming. The yard has lots of tables and shady places to sit and is very comfortable even though temperature was 30ish. What a great place to spend an hour or two.  It's well worth the drive from Edmonton. We had lunch crepes and they were divine.  The staff was very friendly and efficient. The prices are not cheap but the quality of the food was excellent. I didn't see it posted but I heard that all utensils and dishes used are compostable. I plan to return a couple more times this summer.

Crepe and shake Cafe is Beaumont's best kept secret for a seasonal, outdoor cafe. (May-Oct) Crepes are their specialty, but many families stop by for ice cream, shakes, lattes etc. Dessert crepes with seasonal fruit are my favourite. Cheery staff,large&lovely garden seating,family friendly. A great country drive destination! Call ahead for hours.

Amazing little ice cream shop! Definitely worth the short drive into the quaint little town of Beaumont to satisfy your cravings! Skip the overpriced franchises and mass-produced, bland, questionable ingredients and head out to the Crepe and Shake, which features Alberta-made Foothills Creamery ice cream, fresh seasonal fruit, great service and an amazing outdoor dining experience! Very kid friendly and a great place to hang out on these hot summer nights.

Watch for seasonal fruit crepes when they are in. Had a yummy raspberry crepe in July, and now August has fresh peaches from the Okanogan! Addition of new pergola and umbrellas is keeping the garden area nice and shady for those hot days. Watch for the little Duck- it was wandering around and nestled under my foot!

The Crepe & Shake is a cute little seasonal cafe that serves crepes and shakes (as well as other drinks and ice cream). It's located on a residential street, and is actually located at someone's house. You go up to the side of the garage to place your order (there's a sliding window). 

They have several different types of crepes, both savoury and sweet. I got the Thomas Crepe, which had nutella (yum) and strawberries. It was pretty hot outside and in retrospect a warm, freshly made crepe in +30C weather probably wasn't the wisest decision (they have Foothills ice cream too), but the crepe was delicious. Being slightly lactose intolerant I didn't want to have a shake with my crepe, so I just got a pop. 

The crepe was yummy and the price was decent (about $6). This was a nice dessert/snack, but I'd love to come back and try one of the savoury crepes for lunch. 

The Crepe & Shake is a seasonal restaurant (only open from May to October Tuesday-Saturday and there hours vary depending on the weather - best to check their website http://crepeandshakecafe.ca/c'mon_over). There isn't indoor seating, it's all outside, but there's some seating under a gazebo. If it's rainy or cool you might want to bring an umbrella/jacket or get your crepe to go.
great service, great cuts of meat.  Would give a star more but peperoni is not good.

Honestly the worst bytchet I've ever gone to. Forgot about my order for months and I had to call continuously to grey my order and it was still not ready until 2 months after he said bit would be. The staff and owner are rude and do have weak customer service skills and that's being generous. When we spoke with the shop about when we can pick up the order he said he would be here on a Monday , we explained we are coming from north Edmonton and we were garenteed he would be there, however after driving all the way to the shop he was not there and did not answer the phone so we wasted the trip out. I will never ever be back worst experience I've ever had.

All I needed to read was "crepe and shake" to know that I had to visit! If you're in the area near the airport it's a very easy drive over to Beaumont to this place. 

A group of young teenagers were running the show in what seemed to be part of a little private residence. The grounds had sitting areas all over to make you feel like you're right at home! 

I got the maintenance man crepe which was delicious! It had ham and cheese in a crepe, folded up so o could eat it with one hand. 

I also got a chocolate coconut shake that was perfectly blended and neither flavor was too overwhelming. 

Great little place!

Best donairs around, especially with the garlic sauce! Made & served with love! We loved going here when we lived nearby, we now live in the US, but make a point of eating there whenever we're in town!

Our family tried Maina`s Donair today. When you first enter it feels warm, friendly and open with a bright yellow paint and wood log type counter and a tv in the corner for the sports fans. Hubby ordered their super beef donair with peppers while my daughter ordered a regular beef and I ordered a Chicken Donair. 

A bit surprised the donairs weren`t a bit bigger, they were completely stuffed full, so maybe a bigger pita may have served a bit better to be able to wrap the filling. They give you a choice of Garlic, Tzaziki or sweet sauce. I chose Garlic at their suggestion, and have to say it was the best choice. I haven`t heard of any other place using garlic sauce on their donairs, but this was the best chicken donair i have tasted. And even tho the pita was small i was completely full by the end of it. 

Hubby and i also had a bite of each others` as he had ordered the super beef with peppers and Tzazki sauce. I myself wasn`t as impressed, as with my chicken, but think the tzaziki just didn`t do the beef justice like the garlic did the chicken. The peppers were a nice add, giving it a bit of kick without dominating the flavor of the donair. 

They also offer Backlava (not sure if it was homemade or not) which we got but haven`t tried just yet, and bottled pop.

We will go back, we had a nice drive out to Beaumont and found a great little place to stop for a bite and a break:)

Great locally owned cafe with delicious daily soups and sandwiches made from scratch. There's a variety of loose leaf teas, specialty coffees, and the cafe is even licensed.
